newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr near 7-1/2 year highs; Paris, Frankfurt up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr near 7-1/2 year highs; Paris, Frankfurt up.

text.p: The dollar paused for breath on Monday just below a seven-and-a-half year high against the mark set overnight, bolstered by prospects of a weak European single currency and sound U.S. economic growth.
In equity markets, the stronger dollar, seen as helping some European exporters, propelled Paris briefly to a new trading high and drove Frankfurt up by 1.25 percent. But London was lacklustre.
Most of the excitement was in the currency exchanges where the dollar was trading one pfennig higher, at 1.8461 marks, than the levels seen in late European deals on Friday.

A growing conviction that Europe's planned economic and monetary union will be launched by a broad group of countries, making for a soft euro, has helped the dollar rise against the mark as traders switch to safe haven currencies.
The added impetus behind Monday's surge was market expectations that Germany's Bundesbank would not act soon to curb the mark's weakness.

Signs that the American economy is growing without stoking inflation has generated demand for U.S. stocks and bonds, and helped the dollar gain against other major currencies like the Swiss franc and the yen.
"There has been a shift from the mark weakness story to an independent dollar strength story, and people are going to stick to this trend," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
"We will doubtless get the threat of intervention and rhetoric out of Germany but the Bundesbank is unlikely to hike the repo rate unless the dollar is travelling at speed above 1.90 (marks)."

The dollar soared to 1.8470 marks in Asian trade overnight, its strongest point since November 1989 when it reached 1.8690. The U.S. currency also leapt to 1.5250 Swiss francs, its best showing since August 1993.
The dollar eased back slightly against the mark by the European mid-morning but was at 117.26 yen, half a yen higher than its level on Friday.
Bundesbank officials have started dropping hints, directed at currency traders, about the powerful American currency.

Johann Wilhelm Gaddum, vice president of the German central bank, said in an interview last week that the dollar was slightly overvalued. His fellow council member Reimut Jochimsen said the Bundesbank, which did not normally allow exchange rates to dictate its policy, was following them more closely than usual.

"The market does not believe the Bundesbank for a second in terms of its willingness or its ability to support the mark," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.

The strengthening dollar had a knock-on effect on the Frankfurt bourse where stocks climbed 62.24 points to 4379.88 at one stage, boosted by export-led stocks like carmakers and chemicals. Prices fell back slightly later.
Dealers said the market had calmed down after last week's turbulence when a record-breaking run ran out of steam on Friday.
The prospect of the mark weakening further should continue to inderpin the stock market but the likelihood of temporary setbacks is growing, analysts said.

"Signs of interim technical corrections have strengthened recently but the corrections should be limited. Weak days therefore continue to be suited to appropriate portfolio increases," analysts at Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG wrote in a note to investors.
Electrical giant Siemens AG rose almost five percent to a new year high of 131.60 marks, gaining from positive analysts' assessments in the wake of nine-month results published last week.
Paris climbed 15 points to hit a new trading peak of 3044.24, buoyed by the stronger dollar, but investor sentiment soon turned negative and the bourse shed most of the gains.

In London, stocks slipped in and out of profit in early trading, and dealers said the market lacked direction ahead of a batch of major corporate results due later in the week. Wall Street, which closed down a few points on Friday, offered no guidance.
"We have a lot of results later this week," said one senior dealer. "In typical Monday fashion I expect we'll lack direction and volumes will be quite low."
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8461 marks and 117.26 yen compared to 1.8350 and 116.75 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index down 0.6 points at 4,850.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 58.26 points in bourse trade at 4,375.90.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 4.09 points at 3,030.03.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $325.40 an ounce compared to Friday's close of $324.05. Silver was four cents stronger at $4.36.
